name: Mealtime Routine
subtitle: Requesting & Refusing at the Table
when: Any regular meal or snack time
description: Everyday meals are a rich communication goldmine. This routine captures how your child asks for more of a preferred food, refuses a disliked item, and uses gaze, gesture, or words at the table.
setup: Place 2-3 preferred foods AND 1 non-preferred food within your child's sight but slightly out of reach.
Serve only small portions so they need to ask for more.
Turn off TV/background noise to reduce distractions.

opportunities.label: Request preferred food
opportunities.prompt: Serve a tiny portion of a favourite food. Wait quietly (up to 10 seconds) before offering more — let your child ask first.

opportunities.label: Refuse disliked food
opportunities.prompt: Offer the non-preferred food with a smile. Hold it near and wait 5 seconds to see how your child communicates refusal.

opportunities.label: Comment on meal
opportunities.prompt: Take a big exaggerated bite, say 'Mmm!' then look at your child expectantly — waiting for any shared attention or comment.

opportunities.label: Signal all done
opportunities.prompt: When the child seems finished, gently model 'all done' (hands open) but wait before clearing — observe whether they signal finished.

name: Bath & Sensory Play
subtitle: Requesting actions & water play
when: Bath time or water play session
description: Bath time is a natural laboratory for communication. Water, bubbles, and bath toys create irresistible motivation to request actions, protest stops, and share excitement.
setup: Prepare a cup for pouring water as a fun repeated action.
Keep a dry towel nearby to pause activities intentionally.

opportunities.label: Request water pour
opportunities.prompt: Pour water from a cup over child's hands — they'll likely love it! Pour once, then hold the cup up and wait. Do they ask for more?

opportunities.label: Protest stop of favourite action
opportunities.prompt: Mid-splash or mid-pour, suddenly stop and look away. Wait 8 seconds. Does the child protest, reach, or use any communication to resume?

opportunities.label: Bubble pop anticipation
opportunities.prompt: Blow a bubble near child, then pause before the next one. Does child show anticipation — looking at wand, vocalising, reaching?

opportunities.label: Choose a bath toy
opportunities.prompt: Hold up two bath toys, one in each hand, and wait — don't name them. Which one does the child choose and how do they indicate their preference?

name: Dressing & Getting Ready
subtitle: Requesting help & protesting wrong choices
description: Getting dressed involves real, functional communication needs — asking for help, refusing the wrong item, and choosing between options. It's a perfect routine-embedded teaching moment.
setup: Have 2 different shirt or sock options visible.
Intentionally get one item 'wrong' (e.g., put shoe on head or sock on hand).
Leave a zipper or button undone so child may request help.

opportunities.label: Request help with clothing
opportunities.prompt: Start putting on a shoe but don't finish fastening it. Wait — does the child indicate they need help (extend foot, vocalise, point, word)?

opportunities.label: Protest wrong item
opportunities.prompt: Put the sock on the wrong foot, or put a hat on your own head saying 'Yours!' — observe whether child communicates the error.

opportunities.label: Choose between two items
opportunities.prompt: Hold up two socks or two shirts. 'This one or that one?' — wait for any deliberate choice signal.

opportunities.label: Label a clothing item
opportunities.prompt: Hold up an item and ask 'What's this?' — pause for up to 10 seconds before naming it yourself.

name: Bedtime Storytime
subtitle: Joint attention, pointing & labeling
description: Shared reading is one of the most powerful language-building activities. This routine measures index-finger pointing at pictures, joint gaze, picture labeling, and turn-taking in a cozy, low-stress setting.
setup: Choose a simple picture book with clear, colourful images on each page.
Sit side-by-side or child on lap so you share the same view.
Read only 2-3 pages per opportunity and pause at interesting pictures.

opportunities.label: Point to picture on request
opportunities.prompt: Point to a picture and ask 'Where's the dog?' — wait for child to look, point, or vocalise before moving on.

opportunities.label: Spontaneous picture labeling
opportunities.prompt: Turn to a new page, wait 6 seconds before naming anything. Does the child spontaneously comment, point, or label?

opportunities.label: Request page turn
opportunities.prompt: Pause at the end of a page and wait — does the child indicate they want to continue? (reaching for page, vocalising, gaze to parent)

opportunities.label: Share excitement about story
opportunities.prompt: React with exaggerated surprise to a picture ('Oh no! The bear!') and look at child — do they share the excitement back?
